rules_evaluated.evidence: L17-19 closest to violating: 'No cheap verifier? Keep the task, or build the verifier first and then delegate... Every verifier you write converts one more task family from delegation-trap to delegation-win.' Stays inside — this is the conceptual handoff a between-module pre-read owes: it primes M5's 'Build the verifier. First eval, named' move without doing that teaching itself (no verifier-construction walkthrough, no eval mechanics), and it is read while the M4 send-off is already running (strategy doc L434, run-the-first-experiment.md L71-78), so it cannot pre-empt M4's un-packaged-run requirement either. Sets up 'learning through contrast' (M5's mood) without resolving it. Read while the un-packaged run is loose in the room, closest thing to a teaching beat here rather than pure setup, so the mood floor is the relevant test and it clears.

L12 closest to violating: 'You saved the writing and bought a harder review. The full cost comes back to you at read time.' Reads as an economic consequence of a task-class choice, not a verdict on something the student did wrong — no 'you should have', no address to a specific past action of the student's. Body never frames unease as having-done-wrong; the piece's only affect is diagnostic (name the verifier or don't have one), matching theme #1's not-knowing register.
